answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set whose backs match that color; remove cards targeting colors not in play, but keep that player's own Ambush card. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Each player chooses a color and stands its Player ID card visibly in front of them'; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their face-down card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'There is no individual turn order.' Vote: 'You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed' and 'reveal all choices simultaneously.'

answers.answer: No. A four-vote majority is not necessary. The player or players receiving the most votes are the Target(s), even if the leading total is only three of seven; in this case Red is the sole Target with three votes.
answers.evidence: Vote: 'The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.'

answers.answer: With Red and Blue tied for the most votes, both are Targets. Since neither uses Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to any other applicable rule (including Ambush effects).
answers.evidence: Vote: tied leaders are all Targets; 'With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.'

answers.answer: No. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive. Green voted for Red, not the sole Target Blue, so Green did not vote for a Target and is eliminated, absent a successful Ambush exception; Green did not Ambush.
answers.evidence: Vote: 'Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated'; the successful Ambush exception is specified separately.

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so Red's Ambush adds no vote; among the specified votes, Red gets Yellow's vote and Yellow gets Pink's vote, one each. The question does not specify the other players' votes, so the overall vote totals, actual Target(s), and resulting survivors cannot be determined. If Red is a Target, Red's Ambush succeeds and Red may eliminate one player who voted for Red; Yellow is a legal choice. Pink, who voted for Yellow, is not a legal choice for Red's retaliation. If Red is not a Target, Red's Ambush fails and Red eliminates themself.
answers.evidence: Vote: 'Ambush cards do not count as votes.' Ambush: it works only if its player is a Target and lets them choose 'one of the players who voted for them'; a non-Target ambusher eliminates themself.

answers.answer: No. A successful ambusher chooses one of the four players who voted for them to eliminate, not all four. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: a successful ambusher 'chooses one of the players who voted for them'; they 'cannot choose ... someone who voted for a different Target.'

answers.answer: The Ambush fails, and that player eliminates themself.
answers.evidence: Ambush: 'An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.'

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among those surviving players; only survivors participate in subsequent votes.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: 'Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.'

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Those four cards are not necessarily four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, and their values vary.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: one survivor 'collects all four central Gold Bars'; Components says bar values are 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of three cards—Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go—may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes 'Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go'; they may discuss, choose one face down, and reveal both choices simultaneously when ready.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, including those eliminated by it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave all four there for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: 'Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.' Edge cases: final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: 'You get 2; opponent gets 2.'

answers.answer: The Steal player receives all four central Gold Bar cards; the Share player receives none.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: Share player gets 0; Steal player gets 4.

answers.answer: The Steal player receives three central Gold Bar cards and the Grab One & Go player receives one.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: Grab One & Go player gets 1; Steal player gets 3.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives three central Gold Bar cards and the Share player receives one.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Grab One & Go: Share player gets 3; Grab One & Go player gets 1.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two bars remain in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars to the center for the next round.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, 'each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.'

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: on double Steal, 'neither finalist receives gold'; give 'every other player one Gold Bar from the deck'; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: check 'at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded'; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; 'the highest point total wins.'

answers.answer: For exactly two qualifying players tied for the highest Gold point total, the booklet requires a Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player has the highest total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round. The summary notes the booklet does not provide a procedure for three or more tied leaders, but that limitation does not apply to the stated two-player tie.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied highest qualifying totals 'conduct another Final Showdown' and repeat as necessary until a single player has the highest total. Turn Structure: 'everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.'
